title: Relative dynamic orbit, coaction-weight and base-change interfaces
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Work in schemes over $S$ [def-pc-scheme], with group objects and group homomorphisms as in [def-sc-group-scheme], using $S$ in place of the field base. Write $T(B)=\operatorname{Spec}B\to S$ for a commutative $A$-algebra $B$, $L=\operatorname{Spec}A[t]$, and $M=\operatorname{Spec}A[t,t^{-1}]$ with its Laurent Hopf group law [def-sfb-split-torus-over-ring]. Let $j:M\to L$ be the unit-locus inclusion and $0,1:S\to L$ be evaluation sections. A group $H$ has an action by automorphisms if an internal $M$-action satisfies $s\cdot(xy)=(s\cdot x)(s\cdot y)$ on every test $S$-scheme. For $h:T\to H$, a contracting orbit extension is $e:L\times_ST\to H$ whose restriction along $j\times\mathrm{id}_T$ is $(s,t)\mapsto s\cdot h(t)$ and whose restriction at zero is the identity point. Define $\operatorname{Attracts}_H(h)$ by the existence of this extension. A homomorphism $i:U\to H$ represents this subfunctor if, for every $T$ and $h$, $\operatorname{Attracts}_H(h)$ is equivalent to the existence of a unique $x:T\to U$ with $i\circ x=h$. Use the existing dual-number tangent module $\operatorname{Lie}(H)$ and its tangent points [sk-d-tangent], valid over $A$. The image of the tangent inclusion consists of the vectors whose dual-number points factor through $i$. The tangent map of a group homomorphism is obtained by composing infinitesimal points and using the canonical Lie-to-infinitesimal-point equivalence. Define homogeneous functions of degree $j$ by $f(a(t,h))=t^j f(h)$ as an equality of regular functions on $M\times_S H$. Define the tangent coefficient of $f$ at a tangent vector by the epsilon coefficient of its pullback to $A[\epsilon]$. The coaction weight submodule $\mathfrak h_j$ is the span of tangent vectors annihilating all homogeneous functions of degrees other than $j$. Put $\mathfrak h_{>0}=\sum_{j>0}\mathfrak h_j$. A group $U$ has unipotent geometric fibres when, for every algebraically closed $A$-field $F$, its base change [def-pc-base-change] to $F$ admits a faithful closed group representation [def-weil-closed-immersion] in some $\mathrm{GL}_{n,F}$ [def-sc-general-linear-group] whose every $F$-point $x$ satisfies $(r(x)-1)^N=0$ for some $N$. Allow $n=0$. For a ring map $A\to B$, use the canonical pullback functor on group objects and its map on homomorphisms. A point of $H_B$ viewed over $A$ is the image under the canonical pullback adjunction. Define representing the attracting functor after this base change by the same unique-factorization condition for these points and the pulled-back inclusion. Finally, for an $A$-algebra $B$, a tangent comparison is a $B$-linear equivalence $e_H:B\otimes_A\operatorname{Lie}(H)\to\operatorname{Lie}(H_B)$ whose value on $1\otimes v$, projected to $H$, is the tangent point of $v$ precomposed with $\operatorname{Spec}(A[\epsilon]\to B[\epsilon])$. Thus its values on all pure tensors are fixed.
